clue.text: Eastern thinker retreats into the abstract

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the letters are read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for east or eastern
one who muses, or ponders

explanation.surface: A philosopher from the East withdraws into pure abstraction.
explanation.walkthrough: EMUSER read backwards gives RESUME; 'the abstract' looks like philosophy but is the summary of a document.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstract is a short summary of a longer paper, which is what a résumé also is.

clue.text: About a hundred balls used in rallies

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
C is the Roman numeral for 100
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled

explanation.surface: Tennis or cricket balls in long exchanges of play.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the British bat-and-ball game, an over is six deliveries, so balls can mean overs. 'Rallies' suggests tennis, but here it is the verb meaning gets better.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to regain strength or health, and a patient who rallies recovers.

clue.text: Bribed a few men who accept a note

indicators.note: those who accept something take it in, so one group holds the other inside it

blocks.note: a squad is a small group of soldiers or players
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Some men were paid off by taking banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A note' looks like money, which fits bribery, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To square someone is informal for securing their compliance, often by a payment or bribe.

clue.text: Plant with mottled appearance hidden by a girl gardener

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing is enclosed within it

blocks.note: chiné is a fabric woven with a mottled, clouded pattern
the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow?'

explanation.surface: A speckled plant concealed by a young woman tending her garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks botanical, which suits the gardener, but it means industrial equipment. Chiné is a dress fabric with a clouded, mottled weave.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant is a collective word for the machines and heavy equipment used in industry or construction.

clue.text: Houseboy's back — he's in Hamlet

indicators.note: going back means the boy's name is written from its last letter to its first

blocks.note: read as house plus boy: a villa is a large house, and Reg is a boy's name, short for Reginald

explanation.surface: A servant boy turns up as a character in Shakespeare's Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Houseboy splits into house and boy, and only the boy's name is turned back. Hamlet looks like Shakespeare's play, but a hamlet is a small village.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamlet is a little village, and someone living in one is a villager.

clue.text: With deputed authority to place in irons arbitrarily

indicators.note: arbitrarily means in a random way, so the order of these letters is unpredictable

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An official with delegated power may shackle prisoners at will.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase means 'in the place of a parent', used of teachers or guardians acting for parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A school acting for absent parents holds authority handed over to it, which is what deputed authority means.

clue.text: Speed restriction, maybe, for motorway with lights all round

indicators.note: with here means accompanied by being placed within, surrounded as the next words say
all round means encircling, so one piece goes completely around the other

blocks.note: lights, as in sets alight, has past tense lit
the M1, Britain's first long motorway, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A speed limit on a motorway with lights all along it.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed restriction is one example of a limit, a maximum that must not be exceeded.

clue.text: One who loves to irritate a soldier, perhaps

blocks.note: to gall is to annoy
a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so ant is an example of a soldier

explanation.surface: A romantic who enjoys annoying a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier, perhaps' is a soldier ant, not a person in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A gallant is an old word for a lover or suitor, a man paying attentions to a lady.

clue.text: Fight is a breach of the peace

indicators.note: a breach breaks into something, so one word is pushed into the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written
rest is peace and quiet

explanation.surface: Starting a fight is treated as a breach of the peace in law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breach of the peace' reads as a set phrase, a British public-order offence, but 'breach' is the instruction to break in.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or oppose something, struggling against it.

clue.text: She was represented by each side in 4 provincial capitals

definitions.text: She was represented by each side in 4

blocks.clueFragment: She was represented by each side in 4
blocks.note: first meaning: the queen whose royal cipher was VR, the outer letters of the answer to 4 across
second meaning: two Canadian provincial capitals, of British Columbia and Saskatchewan

explanation.surface: A woman is depicted on both flanks of four regional capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: The cipher VR stood for Queen Victoria; the outer letters of VILLAGER are V and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin title of the queen who reigned 1837 to 1901 also names two Canadian cities that are seats of provincial government.

clue.text: Amateur bricklayer building badly

blocks.note: a church is a kind of building
ill as an adverb means badly, as in 'ill-treated'

explanation.surface: A hobbyist bricklayer is making a poor job of the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Winston Churchill famously laid bricks as a hobby at Chartwell, his country house, so 'Amateur bricklayer' points to him.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime prime minister was a keen hobby bricklayer, building garden walls at his Kent home.

clue.text: Great distance covered by Captain Standish

blocks.note: first meaning: a long way
second meaning: the first name of the Mayflower's military leader

explanation.surface: A long journey made by a famous Pilgrim soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Myles (or Miles) Standish was the military adviser to the Pilgrim Fathers who sailed on the Mayflower in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of a unit of length is used loosely for a large distance, and it is also the Pilgrim captain's forename.

clue.text: Composer initially comes to a decision

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: Giuseppe Verdi, the Italian opera composer
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A composer finally makes up his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's verdict is its formal decision on the case, and the word is used for any judgement reached.

clue.text: Weapon injured girl

blocks.note: cut as in wounded
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: An armed attack has left a girl hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, the type traditionally carried by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: A cold place, but not noisy, a mountain-top

indicators.note: but not means leave out the following item from what came before

blocks.note: a fridge is a place kept cold
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A cold, quiet summit is described.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIDGE without F gives RIDGE. In music f (forte) means loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow crest of a mountain or range of hills, its top line.

clue.text: Censure a town for extortion

blocks.note: a rap is a rebuke, to rap is to criticise
taken as written
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A town is criticised for squeezing money out of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapacity is grasping greed, the urge to seize what belongs to others, so it suits extortion loosely.

clue.text: Scorn not my clue - it's soluble

indicators.note: something soluble dissolves and can be reformed, so these letters break up and settle in a new order

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A setter dismissing criticism: don't sneer at my clue, it can be solved.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumely is insolent contempt, scornful abuse in speech or behaviour.

clue.text: As the procrastinator says. I'm a fan

blocks.note: a putter-off's motto

explanation.surface: Someone who puts things off cheerfully admits to being a supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into three words, the answer is what a procrastinator always says: I do later.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships idols, and loosely is a devoted admirer, a fan of some star.

clue.text: Stick to the rules with faint praise from drama critic

blocks.note: first meaning: behave honestly in a game
second meaning: a reviewer judging a stage show merely all right

explanation.surface: A critic plays by the rules but damns a production with lukewarm words.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a critic's verdict, the phrase means 'the play was fair', which is faint praise indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to act honestly and within the rules, and read literally it is a theatre review calling a show middling.

clue.text: The French show fight at sea

blocks.note: le is French for the
a panto, pantomime, is a British Christmas stage show

explanation.surface: The French put on a show of naval combat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Lepanto in 1571 was a great naval engagement in which the Holy League defeated the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: 27 in number, seeing red

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
to see red is to be furious, mad

explanation.surface: A wanderer in a numbered group is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: the answer to 27 across, a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad roams from place to place with no fixed home, just like a hobo or other itinerant.

clue.text: Sarcastic chap goes round ring road to the West End

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it on both sides
the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: a chap is a man
O is ring-shaped
Rd is the abbreviation for road
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A cutting man drives round the ring road into London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but asks for the last letter of West.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is biting and caustic, so a mordant remark is a sarcastic one.

clue.text: A hybrid type of clue

blocks.note: taken as written
a cross is a hybrid, the offspring of two breeds

explanation.surface: A clue that mixes two different kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is self-referential: crossword clues come as across or down.
explanation.definitionFit: In a crossword the clues are grouped as across or down, so across names one class of clue.

clue.text: Sudden change of mind about value

blocks.note: ca, circa, is the abbreviation for about, used with dates
the price of something is its value

explanation.surface: Someone abruptly rethinks what something is worth.
explanation.definitionFit: A caprice is a whim, an impulsive and unaccountable shift of mood or decision.

clue.text: For help with national insurance rise, see this paper

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading upwards, from the last letter back to the first

blocks.note: aid is help
NI stands for National Insurance, the UK's social security contribution

explanation.surface: Advice to read a certain newspaper for help with rising National Insurance payments.
explanation.walkthrough: AIDNI read upwards gives INDIA. 'This paper' looks like the newspaper, but India paper is a very thin printing paper.
explanation.definitionFit: India paper is a thin, tough, opaque paper used for Bibles and dictionaries.

clue.text: Not fighting gear

blocks.note: first meaning: taking no side in a war
second meaning: the position of a gearbox where no gear is engaged

explanation.surface: Equipment for those who are staying out of the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A country standing aside from a war is non-aligned, and the car's gearstick has a disengaged position of that name.

clue.text: Had confessed

blocks.note: first meaning: possessed
second meaning: admitted

explanation.walkthrough: 'Had confessed' reads as one past-perfect verb, but it splits into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of own means possessed, and to own something can also mean to acknowledge or admit it.

clue.text: Fashions aren't in it for a hobo

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters that follow are shaped anew

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Clothing styles are irrelevant to a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like the subject noun, but it is a verb telling you to remake the next letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is an American tramp who travels about looking for work, a travelling person with no settled home.

clue.text: Fare dodger was confused about closed road

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of their order
about means going around, so the jumbled letters surround the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
a door that is to is shut
a way is a road

explanation.surface: A passenger without a ticket got muddled over a road closure.
explanation.walkthrough: Closed as 'to' is an old usage, as in 'push the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides aboard a ship or plane to travel without paying for a ticket.

clue.text: Native boys, terrified, hide

indicators.note: the words hide the answer within them, concealing it across a word break

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Local lads, scared stiff, go into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: A native is an oyster raised in British beds, especially at Whitstable in Kent; 'Native' looks like a local person.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives is the trade name for oysters bred in British waters, prized above imported ones.
